messages:
alex: quick post-rfc note: we need a concrete proposal for rollout metadata that balances rollbacks, disk growth, and runtime routing. artifact-only vs lease-only feels polarizing.

maria: agreed. artifact-only wins for reproducibility (you always know exactly what binary/hash was served), but storage + retention headache is real.

daan: lease-only is operationally friendly: runtime can evict when idle, cheaper for Dedicated. downer is you lose immutable provenance unless we also record artifact snapshots elsewhere.

tess: what about a small hybrid: canonical artifact ids for provenance and short-lived "placement leases" for runtime placement and GC. manifests point to artifact ids; leases reference manifests.

alex: that mirrors what folks sketched today, but we should decide a few hard points: (1) should manifests be intentionally tiny so clients can cache? (2) are leases opaque tokens or predictable strings? (3) what fields are required for safe fallbacks?

maria: answers: (1) yes, manifests tiny. keep only artifact_id, semantic_tag, compat_labels, and one-line telemetry keys. (2) leases = opaque UUIDs. keeps revocation simple. (3) include a compatibility hint list plus an optional fallback_artifact array.

daan: add runtime-only hints to leases: placement_hint (gpu_type), prefer_warm (bool), lease_ttl_seconds. These are advisory but help autoscaler.

tess: we also need to record a minimal quality signal in manifest so runtime prefers higher-quality fallbacks: e.g., eval_score: "0.82". numeric string ok for the thread doc.

alex: sketch manifest example (small):

```
artifact_id: sha256:8f2b...
semantic_tag: prod-2026-03
compat_labels: ["chat-v2", "embed-v1"]
eval_score: 82
release_channel: stable
deprecated: false
```

maria: and a lease example (runtime object, not client-facing):

```
lease_id: urn:lease:3a2b...
artifact_id: sha256:8f2b...
tenant_id: tenant-123
placement_hint: a100
prefer_warm: true
ttl_seconds: 43200
created_at: 2026-03-19T08:00:00Z
```

daan: operational note: leases should be stored in a small KV with TTL support; when a lease expires, GC considers artifact unreachable unless another lease or retention policy references it.

tess: GC policy proposal: keep artifact if (1) referenced by any active lease OR (2) created within retention_window_days OR (3) pinned_by_customer flag = true. otherwise candidate for deletion.

alex: on client resolution: client GET /manifests/:semantic_tag or :artifact_id. servers return tiny manifest; client caches short (e.g., 60s) and falls back to server-directed resolution if missing. runtime uses leases to choose placement; if selected pool lacks artifact, runtime consults compat_labels to select fallback artifacts ordered by eval_score.

maria: important: any fallback that could materially change model behavior must trigger a telemetry event with fields {requested_artifact, served_artifact, lease_id, reason}. Customers can subscribe to these events.

daan: we should also include a "confidence_tier" enum on manifest (HIGH|MEDIUM|LOW) derived from eval_score thresholds. simplifies runtime decisions without comparing floats everywhere.

tess: docs + migration: we need a small shim that writes manifests for existing pinned deployments and backfills leases for active clusters so GC doesn't nuke things.

ops-bot: Card created REDWOOD-2034: implement hybrid manifest + lease system. Assignees: maria, daan, tess.

alex: thanks. can we lock on fields by Friday? if no objections I'll merge manifest proto into the rfc repo and open implementation spikes.

maria: locking Friday works for me.

daan: fine. I'll prototype lease store behaviour this week.

tess: I'll draft the fallback telemetry schema.

alex: perfect. closing for now but follow-up in the RFC PR please.
